# POC Studio Live: skill-improvement loop

## Requested outcome
Gate feedback, human and judge, is already captured in the `psl_feedback` rows the build run reports. This change closes the loop the request asks for: an automation runs every week, groups the open feedback per skill, and writes a prompt improvement suggestion; on the Feedback page a manager sees the suggestion beside the skill's current prompt with its evidence, approves it, and the skill's version moves. Skill versions are tracked as `psl_skill` and `psl_skill_suggestion` records, both already created and seeded.

## Touches
- automation · POC Studio Live · Suggest skill improvements · new
- automation · POC Studio Live · Approve skill suggestion · new
- code-app · POC Studio Live · app-79ea7266eab9

## Contract
- automation · create · POC Studio Live · Suggest skill improvements: scheduled once a week (Monday, 09:00, time zone Asia/Kolkata), one run at a time. For each `psl_skill`: collect the `psl_feedback` rows whose `target_skill` equals the skill's `skill_id`, whose `status` is `open` and whose `created_at` is later than the newest `approved_at` of that skill's approved `psl_skill_suggestion` rows (no approved suggestion means all); skip the skill when it already has a `pending` suggestion or fewer than 3 such tickets; otherwise call the platform automation "Simple Call LLM" (id `66dfd76eb70dad256986b784`, JSON response) with a system prompt that says it improves the prompt of one POC-builder skill from the feedback given on its output and answers a JSON object with `summary` (one sentence) and `proposed_prompt` (the whole new prompt), and as content the skill's current prompt and the tickets' `feedback` texts; parse the answer to an object and write one `psl_skill_suggestion` row: `suggestion_id` `SUG-<skill id>-<epoch ms>`, `skill`, `from_version` the skill's `current_version`, `to_version` one higher, `summary`, `proposed_prompt`, `evidence_count`, `evidence_tickets` (the ticket numbers, comma-separated), `status` `pending`, `created_at` now. A model answer that is not a JSON object with both keys writes nothing for that skill and the run continues with the next skill. Each skill is handled on its own; the run ends with a stop.
- automation · create · POC Studio Live · Approve skill suggestion: callable, called by the Approve button on the Feedback page. Inputs: `suggestion_id` (required), `caller_email`, `caller_name`. Result: `status` one of `approved` `already_decided` `forbidden` `not_found` `error`, `skill_id`, `to_version`, `message`. The caller must be a manager: `caller_email` equals the `manager_email` of at least one `psl_poc` row, or `caller_name` equals a `manager_name` (case-insensitive); otherwise `forbidden`. A suggestion whose status is not `pending` answers `already_decided`. Approving sets the suggestion `approved` with `approved_by` the caller's name and `approved_at` now; sets the `psl_skill` row's `current_version` to `to_version` and `prompt` to `proposed_prompt`; sets each ticket in `evidence_tickets` to status `resolved` with `action_taken` "Included in `<skill name>` v`<to_version>`", `reviewed_by` the caller's name and `resolved_at` now. Writes to existing rows set single fields, never replace the record.
- code-app · update · POC Studio Live: screen Feedback `/feedback`, from design.md: each skill group's summary card gains the current version and a "Suggestion pending" tag and a version list built from the skill's approved suggestions; the pending suggestion is an AI Insight card (current prompt beside the proposed prompt, the evidence tickets as links to the articles below, one Approve button shown only to a manager-viewer, with the five outcome toasts) placed first in the group; the page keeps the source's own words and layout otherwise · reads `psl_skill` `psl_skill_suggestion` `psl_feedback` `psl_poc` · calls "POC Studio Live · Approve skill suggestion" on Approve.

## Business rules
- A suggestion is only ever a proposal: nothing changes a skill's prompt or version until a manager approves it.
- A skill with a pending suggestion gets no second one; approving resolves the evidence tickets, so the same complaint is never counted twice.
- Only a manager (the manager of at least one POC row) can approve; the automation checks it again.
- Every AI-written suggestion is shown in a labelled AI card with one action inside it.
- No secret and no real prompt of the Claude plugin is stored: the skill prompts in the app are the stand-ins that were seeded.

## Ready when
- deploy POC Studio Live · Suggest skill improvements
- deploy POC Studio Live · Approve skill suggestion
- publish POC Studio Live
- One run of the weekly automation on the seeded tickets leaves one pending suggestion for the PRD writer skill and none for the others.
- The Feedback page shows that suggestion with its evidence and an Approve button for a manager.

## Assumptions
- Check this: threshold 3 open tickets per skill since its last approval; weekly cadence on Monday 09:00 Asia/Kolkata; with the seeds this gives one pending suggestion for the PRD writer (5 open tickets) and none for the mockup drafter (2).
- Check this: "admin" is any signed-in manager (the manager of at least one POC row); no admin field, role or group is added.
- Check this: there is no Run now button and no reject action: the request asks for approval only, and the one run on the seeds is made once by the main session after the deploy.
- Check this: the source app's own Feedback page changed after the clone was made (its head moved to 48b64ea4936d2a50c84226619ed74cdc34e78586: "Skills & Feedback" changes); the app task downloads the source again, compares its Feedback screen with the clone's, and keeps the source's newest layout where it does not conflict with design.md.
- The skill rewrite is a node of the weekly automation, not a second AI agent.
